answer: The sky becomes blue because Earth's atmosphere scatters sunlight like a prism, bending it so that blue light shines directly up at us while other colours are bent over our heads. As a result, we only see blue when the sun is near the horizon and see white daylight when the sun is higher overhead. The same light that makes the sky blue can also be concentrated directly in our eyes at noon, making the sun look bright white.
